title: ai_router.answer.v1
description: Answer object emitted by `router.py "prompt" --json`. Exit code semantics: 0 success (text present) · 2 all routes quota-dead or failing · 3 no keys configured at all · 4 invalid providers.json. v2.5.0 adds optional grounding-contract fields (confidence/degraded/truncated/attempts/latency_s/tps); consumers must treat any of them as absent-able.

text.description: The answer text. Present on success.

cached.description: True when served from the local SHA-256 cache (no API call).

error.description: Machine-readable error kind; present only on failure (e.g. 'invalid providers config').

detail.description: Human-readable error detail; present only on failure.

confidence.description: Trust hint 0..1 = measured route quality x learned reliability. Suggested gating: <0.5 regenerate, 0.5-0.75 verify, >0.75 accept. A hint, never a guarantee.

degraded.description: True when the answer came from a fallback (first-choice route(s) failed). Verify before high-stakes use.

truncated.description: True when the provider reported finish_reason=length (answer may be incomplete — extend max_tokens or abstain). null/absent when unknown.

attempts.description: Routes tried before one answered. >3 suggests systemic exhaustion — consider abstaining.

latency_s.description: Wall-clock seconds until the answer completed.

tps.description: Measured output tokens/second (when the transport reported usage).
